description.text: We are a leading broadband connectivity company with services available to 58 million homes and small to large businesses across 41 states through our Spectrum® brand. Founded in 1993, we have evolved from providing cable TV to streaming, and from high-speed Internet to a converged broadband, WiFi and mobile experience. Over the Spectrum Fiber Broadband Network and supported by our 100% U.S.-based employees, we offer Seamless Connectivity and Entertainment with Spectrum Internet®, Mobile, TV and Voice products. Our strategy is focused on utilizing our fiber-powered network to deliver high-quality, competitively priced products, with outstanding service, allowing us to increase both the number of customers we serve over our network and the number of products we sell to each customer. This combination also reduces the number of service transactions we perform per relationship, yielding higher customer satisfaction and lower customer churn, which results in lower costs to acquire and serve customers and drives greater profitability.

about.description_short: Spectrum is a suite of advanced communications services offered by Charter Communications, Inc. (NASDAQ:CHTR), the leading broadband and video company in the nation and the fastest growing mobile provider in its footprint, with services available to more than 70 million homes and small to large businesses across 45 states. Founded in 1993, Charter has evolved from providing cable TV to streaming, and from high-speed Internet to a converged broadband, WiFi and mobile experience. Over the Spectrum Fiber Broadband Network and supported by our 100% U.S.-based employees, the Company offers Seamless Connectivity and Entertainment with Spectrum Internet, Mobile, TV and Voice products.

analysis_md:
# CHTR — Charter Communications, Inc.
Pass-1 run, 2026-10-18 (engine 5.4.0). All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, or financials_history.csv — none are recomputed. Deal and quarter facts marked "search-cited" come from the sources found in this run's web research (Q2 2026 earnings coverage, Cox/Liberty close coverage, Q1 2026 call coverage).

## What it is
US cable operator (Spectrum brand): broadband, video, voice and an MVNO mobile product. FY2025 revenue $54.774B (−0.56% YoY). In scope under $40B — market cap $15.167B at the $110.11 price (nasdaq_quote_api). The defining fact of this run: **on August 19–20, 2026 — after every filing the engine read (latest 10-Q is Q2 2026, filed 2026-07-24) — Charter closed both the $34.5B Cox Communications acquisition and the Liberty Broadband merger** (search-cited). Cox Enterprises received the equivalent of just over 46 million Charter shares and now owns ~26% of the combined company's fully diluted shares; ~$12B of Cox debt and finance leases remains outstanding at Charter subsidiaries; the Liberty leg net-retired ~4.7 million shares. Combined footprint ~70M homes passed across 45 states. None of that is in the financial history below — every per-share figure is pre-merger standalone Charter, and the score must be read that way.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $16,077,000,000; capex $11,659,000,000; SBC $673,000,000 (always a real cost).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $3,745,000,000 = $27.19/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE/share $27.19; latest FY OE total $3.745B)
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): $3,914,000,000 — same ballpark; the conservative OCF-based figure is the one used.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years. Net debt $94.279B (key_numbers.md); total debt $94,756,000,000 on the FY2025 history line.
- The OE series is capex-cycle dominated: OE total ran $8.174B (2021) → $5.079B (2022) → $2.626B (2023) → $2.510B (2024) → $3.745B (2025) as capex climbed from $7.635B to the ~$11.4–12.1B plateau of the DOCSIS 4.0 / network-evolution and rural-build cycle. Management guides capex of ~$11.4B for 2026 (standalone, ex-Cox), falling to below $8B a year only by 2028 (search-cited Q1/Q2 2026 call coverage).

**TTM through Q2 2026, from ttm.py (filing-direct, no hand math) — computed, then rejected as the base (see BASE_DIVERGENCE):**
- OCF: FY $16,077,000,000 − prior YTD $7,836,000,000 + current YTD $8,229,000,000 = **TTM $16,470,000,000**
- Capex: FY $11,659,000,000 − prior YTD $5,273,000,000 + current YTD $5,726,000,000 = **TTM $12,112,000,000**
- SBC: FY $673,000,000 − prior YTD $379,000,000 + current YTD $341,000,000 = **TTM $635,000,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **123,969,262**
- **TTM OE total $3,723,000,000 → $30.03/share**

**Base used = the engine's normalized base: median of the last 3 FY OE/share = $17.28/share** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share). Its capex leg (~$11.1–11.3B in 2023–24) matches the guided 2026 plateau; its OCF leg is trough-side, which is the conservative direction given the leverage. The method range this creates is the headline — see Thoughts.

## Moat: 4/10 — weak, eroding
Justification: local cable footprint scale and converged broadband+mobile bundling still give pricing power and low churn, but fiber overbuilds and fixed wireless are taking subscribers outright, video is in secular decline, mobile rides on a rival's network (MVNO), and ROIC has only run ~9% — barely above the cost of capital, not wide-moat evidence.
- FOR: scaled local footprint — largest US cable operator after the Aug 2026 Cox close, ~70M homes passed (search-cited deal coverage); converged bundle — Spectrum Mobile grew to 12.5M lines (+406k lines in Q2 2026, search-cited), raising switching friction; operating margin expanded from 17.5% (2020) to 23.6% (2025) on cost discipline despite flat revenue (fundamentals.json); DOCSIS 4.0 network evolution to multi-gig symmetrical speeds defends the core product.
- AGAINST: fiber overbuild + fixed wireless — internet customers fell 172,000 in Q2 2026, −515,000 YoY, and revenue fell −1.7% YoY, the fourth straight shrinking quarter (search-cited); ROIC proxy only 8.91% / 9.38% / 9.04% in 2023 / 2024 / 2025 (fundamentals.json `roic_proxy`) — a thin spread over the cost of capital, which is why this is not a 7+; video in secular decline and broadband ARPU falling under retention promotions (search-cited); mobile is an MVNO on T-Mobile's network — the growth leg rides on a competitor's asset; extreme leverage (net debt $94.279B pre-Cox) leaves no room to answer a price war.
- Evidence note: Charter's filings do not present a gross-profit line (fundamentals.json gross margin is null for every year), so the margin evidence is the operating-margin trend above. ROIC history does not support a high moat: 6.80% (2020) rising to the ~9% plateau of 2022–25 — improvement, but never wide-moat territory through the cycle.
- A 4 gives CAP = 7.2 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 7.2 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-18)
**Growth recalibration (written reason):** the engine's blended growth is 6.55%, and it is not usable as printed. Its components (key_numbers.md: rev CAGR 5y 2.63%, rev CAGR 3y 0.46%, latest rev YoY −0.56%, OE/share CAGR 2y 25.41%) include a +5.00pp buyback adjustment laid over flat-to-declining revenue, and a 25.41% OE/share CAGR that is a capex-cycle artifact off the 2023 trough base — not a growth rate this business prints. The actual recent prints: FY2025 revenue −0.56%, Q2 2026 revenue −1.7% YoY with adjusted EBITDA −4.3% YoY (search-cited). Scenario starts were therefore set in absolute terms via offsets (−0.12548 / −0.08548 / −0.05548 / −0.02548 / +0.01452 vs g_base) to −6 / −2 / **+1** / +4 / +8%. The +1% base start — above the current revenue prints, deliberately — rests on the guided capex step-down (below $8B/yr by 2028, search-cited) mechanically lifting OE inside the fade window and on the at-least-$800M run-rate Cox synergy estimate (search-cited Q1 2026 call coverage), offset by subscriber losses and the post-merger share step-up. Probabilities were shifted bearish to 15/30/30/15/10 (45% bear-or-worse) for the leverage and the secular decline; OE multipliers are the defaults 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25. Price $110.11.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | −6.0% | 0.75 | Fiber/FWA losses accelerate; capex stuck at the plateau; levered OE compresses | $76.34 | 10.93% |
| Bear | 30% | −2.0% | 0.90 | Revenue/EBITDA drift down; Cox integration distracts; buybacks stay off | $107.14 | 14.65% |
| Base | 30% | 1.0% | 1.00 | Subs stabilize slowly; capex step-down from 2028 carries OE/share | $133.74 | 17.72% |
| Bull | 15% | 4.0% | 1.10 | Broadband returns to growth on the upgraded network; synergies land | $165.11 | 21.14% |
| Super bull | 10% | 8.0% | 1.25 | Full capex normalization + synergy + buyback resumption path | $218.50 | 26.48% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $130.33 (+18.4% vs price), IV@12% $171.03, IV@10% $216.20, weighted IRR 17.32%, base-case IRR 17.72%**
- **Tier by numbers: B.** Diagnostics (key_numbers.md): OE yield 15.69%, terminal value 17.6% of IV@15%, scenario spread 2.86x, net debt 39.61x normalized OE, 9.6 months since FY end.
- **Hurdle-clearing prices (weighted path): clears 15% at $130.33, 20% at $93.45, 25% at $72.92.** At $110.11 the name clears the 15% hurdle on the weighted path and does not clear 20%.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest fiscal year ended 9.6 months ago): ttm.py was run through Q2 2026 and its legs are quoted above. The TTM figure was computed and then rejected as the base for the reasons under BASE_DIVERGENCE — the flag is resolved by that decision, not ignored.
- **BUYBACK_TAILWIND** (share count shrinking −5.73%/yr, growth adj 5.00%): the shrink was real pre-merger, but the final scenario starts were set in absolute terms precisely so the verdict does not capitalize a continued −5.73%/yr shrink: the August 2026 Cox issuance stepped the diluted count up by just over 46 million share equivalents (search-cited), and post-close management targets deleveraging to the low end of 3.5–3.75x within three years (search-cited), which competes with buybacks for the same cash. No double count in the verdict.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2023, 2024, 2025): D&A-explained, not a one-off. FY2025 net income $4,987,000,000 vs OCF $16,077,000,000 (financials_history.csv); depreciation/amortization of $8,711,000,000 plus SBC of $673,000,000 bridges most of the gap — cable plant depreciation is non-cash and huge. The OE base is OCF-based throughout, so the divergence does not contaminate it.
- **BASE_DIVERGENCE** (latest FY $27.19 vs 3-yr median $17.28): both are distorted, in opposite directions. The TTM/latest figures capitalize (a) an OCF leg at the high end of its recent range (OCF totals: $14.433B in 2023, $14.430B in 2024, $16.077B in 2025, $16.470B TTM — financials_history.csv / ttm.json) and (b) a share denominator — 123,969,262 current-YTD — that the August 2026 Cox close has already reversed with just over 46 million new share equivalents (search-cited). The median's distortion is the safer one here: its capex leg matches the guided ~$11.4B 2026 plateau (search-cited), and with 39.61x leverage the conservative base is the right one to size on. Median used; the TTM alternative is carried in Thoughts as the method range.
- **HIGH_NET_DEBT** (net debt 39.61x normalized OE): confirmed from the filing — net debt $94.279B, total debt $94,756,000,000 (FY2025), and the Cox close leaves ~$12B more of Cox debt outstanding at Charter subsidiaries (search-cited). This is the central risk of the name: at this leverage a mid-single-digit EBITDA slide moves equity OE violently. Handled by the 45% combined bear-or-worse probability weight and the conservative base; the bear case (IV@15 $107.14) sits essentially at the price.
- **TIER_BAND** (bear tier C at 14.65% vs bull tier A at 21.14%): the verdict spans tiers, so it is sized to the bear end — the final tier is B on the weighted path, with the bear case below the 15% hurdle stated plainly rather than averaged away.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The honest headline is the **method range**: on the normalized median base this is a Tier B (weighted IRR 17.32%, IV@15% $130.33); on the TTM base of $30.03/share from ttm.json the same scenario structure prints Tier S. The entire verdict is the base choice, and the base choice turns on two facts outside the filings: the TTM share denominator was reversed by the Cox issuance in August 2026, and standalone capex stays at the ~$11.4B plateau through 2026 before the guided step-down. Anyone quoting one tier for CHTR without naming its base is hiding the ball.
- A second, larger caveat: **this score is for pre-merger standalone Charter.** The combined company carries ~26% more diluted share equivalents, ~$12B more debt, Cox's own OE stream, and at least $800M of claimed run-rate synergies — none of which is in any filing the engine has read. The first post-merger 10-Q/10-K will move this score materially in one direction or the other; treat this as the standalone anchor, not the combined-company verdict.
- Quality is not the debate: OE positive 5/5 years, operating margin expanding, mobile genuinely growing. The debate is whether a ~9%-ROIC, 39.61x-levered, subscriber-shrinking cableco's OE/share can compound fast enough — via the capex step-down, synergies and eventual buybacks — before fiber and fixed wireless take more of the base. The market price of $110.11 (down from a 52-week range cited in search coverage as $124.05–$422.29 as of June 2026) already prices a lot of the bear case; the bear case here (IV@15 $107.14) agrees with the market, the weighted case sits 18.4% above it.
- Margin of safety: thin. The weighted IV@15% is 18.4% above the price, but the bear IV@15% is below the price and the super-bear IV@15% is $76.34. A buyer here is paid for stabilization plus the capex step-down, and is not insured against the leverage if stabilization fails.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: B** (weighted IRR 17.32% on the normalized median base; method range B to S across the defensible bases, which is itself the finding)
- Confidence: **Low** (base-dominated verdict, TIER_BAND span, 39.61x leverage, and a transformational merger that closed after the latest filing)
- One-liner: Eroding cable moat 4/10 on 39.6x levered OE — clears 15% only on the conservative median base (17.3% weighted, IV $130 vs $110) with a Tier C bear case; the TTM base would print S, so the verdict is base-dominated and sized to the bear end.
